dimensions.name: Reconstructing the Stripe contract & environment

evidence.note: Wrote cards.py (test PANs), errors.py (error envelope), store.py (idempotency), webhooks.py, permissions.py entirely from memory — no doc/SDK-source lookup to reconstruct the contract.

Correctly recalled the hard-part semantics in prose (idempotency scope (api_key,key,body-hash) with per-key locks; PI state machine and capture-succeeded=>400) — but as recollection, not researched grounding.

Installed the real stripe SDK and ran round-trips (declines, idempotency replay, webhook re-signing, concurrency). This grounds the contract against actual SDK behavior, but occurs after building as confirmation rather than probing/reconstruction, and no mismatch reshaped the design.
Final review checklist confirms coverage of envelope/PANs/state-machine, all from the built implementation; no evidence of revisiting external sources as gaps surfaced.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent established the core Stripe contract for all main resources — object shapes, error {type,code,...} mapping, list envelope, test-PAN set — and confirmed SDK/auth compatibility via real stripe SDK round-trips, matching the level-5 anchor. However, all contract knowledge was drawn from memory with zero consultation of Stripe docs or SDK source, and the SDK exercises functioned as post-hoc verification rather than the source-grounded probing and self-correcting reconstruction of the level-8+ anchors. It sits solidly at 5, not higher because no source was ever revisited as gaps arose.

dimensions.name: Sequencing a large surface + three deep traps

evidence.note: Loose design sketch enumerating key behaviors including all three traps (idempotency+locks, card validation, webhook retry) — recognizes traps as distinct but not an ordered milestone hierarchy with done-conditions.

Ring-fences the traps into dedicated modules (store.py=idempotency/locks, webhooks.py=delivery/re-sign, PI state machine flagged at step 23), but build order is infrastructure-first/breadth-first; all code written before any boot.
Boot/skeleton verification happens only AFTER writing the entire codebase — not an early-verifiable auth'd skeleton milestone preceding CRUD, so it misses the [8] front-loading criterion.

Each trap exercised as a distinct workstream (idempotency replay/different-body, capture-succeeded 400, webhook re-sign retry, concurrent serialization) — traps treated as separate, but as verification not pre-planned milestones.
Done-conditions surface as an end-of-run review checklist rather than acceptance conditions attached to each milestone up front.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows clear milestone-ish structure (setup → module build → boot check → trap testing) and distinctly recognizes the three traps, ring-fencing them into separate modules with individual checks — matching the [5] anchor. It falls short of [8] because the build was infrastructure-first rather than risk-front-loaded, the bootable skeleton was verified only after all code was written rather than early, and done-conditions appeared as an end review checklist rather than pre-planned per-milestone acceptance criteria. The ring-fencing and per-trap checks lift it to a solid 5 rather than a flat endpoint checklist ([3]).

dimensions.name: SDK-driven, offline compatibility checks

evidence.note: After booting, ran a structured sequence of targeted curl checks: health, customer CRUD, full PI success flow, decline->402, idempotency replay of a cached error body, same-key-different-body->400 idempotency_error, capture-succeeded->400 payment_intent_unexpected_state, invalid PAN->invalid_number, and missing-auth->401. Covers all three trap semantics plus error/HTTP mappings, well beyond happy-path 200s.

Installed the real `stripe` SDK and verified wire-level compatibility through api_base: customer, payment method, payment intent, refund, decline, subscriptions, products, prices, and restricted-key permission gating (403s) — exactly the SDK-driven verification the 8/10 anchors call for.

Stood up a local HTTP receiver, shrank the retry schedule via env override, triggered an event, and confirmed 5xx retry with exponential backoff AND that each attempt was re-signed (distinct t= values), then checked the deliveries endpoint — the re-signed late-delivery temporal trap from the 10 anchor.
Ran 10 simultaneous same-idempotency-key requests and confirmed all returned the same PaymentIntent ID — directly verifying the serialized-retry/never-double-charge concurrency trap.
Final fresh-boot smoke test with only STRIPE_SK set: verified health and a 404 error envelope, confirming clean default startup before submission.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a deliberate, multi-layer verification harness that exercised routes through the actual `stripe` SDK against api_base and constructed specific checks for every named trap — idempotency replay of a cached error body, same-key-different-body 400, capture-succeeded 400, invalid PAN decline, webhook 5xx retry/backoff with re-signing, plus the two hardest temporal/concurrency traps (10 simultaneous same-key requests never double-charge, distinct re-signed webhook signatures) and restricted-key 403s. That matches the 8 anchor fully and reaches most of the 10 anchor's distinguishing items. It falls just short of a clean 10 because list pagination/starting_after was never explicitly exercised and there was no re-run-after-fix regression loop (though no failures ever arose to trigger one).

dimensions.name: Tracking coverage across a wide surface

evidence.note: Agent enumerated and built every resource family in an ordered pass (customers through restricted keys plus billing/webhook workers), showing an explicit sense of the full surface so no family was omitted.
Systematic verification of trap behaviors (decline 402, idempotency replay/different-body, capture-succeeded 400, invalid_number, no-auth) — coverage-driven testing, not random poking.

Broadened SDK-based verification sweep across subscriptions, products, prices, restricted keys, webhook delivery/retry/re-sign and deliveries — actively confirming the remaining families were exercised.
Final review presents an explicit ✅ checklist across boot/health/auth/error-envelope/cards/state-machine, distinguishing verified requirements — a coverage accounting at the end.
No thrashing or repeated re-debugging occurred, but the smooth run means stuck-detection/time-boxing behavior (the 8-10 markers) was never observably demonstrated.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept an accurate, methodical done-vs-remaining picture: it enumerated all 12+ resource families up front, worked through them without dropping any, verified each trap subsystem, and closed with an explicit coverage checklist — clearly above the '5' anchor's vague tracking. It falls short of '8'+ because the tracking is sequential/implicit rather than a continuously maintained ledger separating implemented-only from verified, and because the clean run never surfaced the stuck-detection/reallocation behaviors that define the top anchors.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on compatibility failures

evidence.note: Server loaded cleanly on first import; all trap behaviors (idempotency replay, different-body 400, decline 402, capture-succeeded 400, invalid_number) passed first try via curl — no failing check occurred that would require course-correction.

SDK round-trips, restricted-key gating, webhook retry/re-signing, and concurrent idempotency all verified successfully on first attempt; no divergence between expectation and result, so no observed revision of the design.
Only observed adaptation: agent recognizes env-var (retry schedule) changes require a server restart and adjusts test procedure — a minor procedural adjustment, not a contract/semantics correction.
Final review and submission proceed without any rework; no falsified assumption surfaced across the horizon, so higher-anchor adaptive behavior is never exercised.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's initial mental model of the Stripe contract proved correct on essentially every test, so no compatibility failure ever forced a course-correction; it never ignored a failing call (ruling out 0-3) but also never demonstrated root-cause diagnosis or propagated model revision (5+/8) because nothing diverged. The lone signal is a minor procedural adjustment at step 39. With no genuine divergences to adapt to, observed adaptive behavior sits low — around 4 — and confidence is low because the dimension was barely exercised.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, high-complexity build: a single-container service that emulates the Stripe REST API at the wire level, faithful enough that the real `stripe` Python SDK works unchanged. Difficulty comes from breadth (12+ resource families, list/error envelopes, restricted keys) AND depth on three explicitly named traps with subtle concurrency/temporal semantics (idempotency replay incl. cached errors and same-key serialization, webhook retry/backoff/re-signing, PaymentIntent state machine), all offline against an external contract the agent must reconstruct. This demands heavy, sustained meta-work: deep research of the real Stripe contract, milestone decomposition across a large surface, SDK-driven verification, progress tracking, and course-correction when compatibility breaks.

dimensions.name: Reconstructing the Stripe contract & environment
dimensions.description: Understanding the externally-defined Stripe wire contract (resource shapes, error codes, test PANs, list/idempotency/webhook semantics) and the SDK's expectations before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The 'spec' is really the real Stripe API; fidelity is graded against SDK behavior the agent must infer, not against this prose. Guessing field names, error codes, or the test-PAN set produces silently non-compliant output.

anchors.0: Starts coding straight from the prompt; invents field names, error codes, and PANs with no reference to actual Stripe behavior.
anchors.3: Recalls a few Stripe shapes from memory; covers the obvious resources but leaves error envelope, list envelope, or PAN set half-guessed.
anchors.5: Establishes the core contract for main resources — object shapes, error `{type,code,...}` mapping, list envelope, the published test-PAN set — and confirms how the SDK sets `api_base`/auth headers before building on them.
anchors.8: Systematically probes the contract for the hard parts too: idempotency key scope `(api_key, key, body)`, webhook signature format, PaymentIntent status transitions, restricted-key scopes — grounded in how the real API/SDK behaves, and revisits sources as gaps surface mid-build.
anchors.10: Sustained, self-correcting reconstruction: cross-checks each subsystem's behavior against concrete SDK round-trips or documented Stripe semantics, catches under-specified corners (decline_code vs code, replay of cached error bodies, re-signing for replay windows) early, and lets findings reshape the design rather than discovering mismatches late.

dimensions.name: Sequencing a large surface + three deep traps
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — auth/boot skeleton, CRUD resources, then the risk-heavy idempotency/webhook/state-machine subsystems — each with a clear done-condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is too large to hold in one push, and the three named traps carry most of the risk; a flat, breadth-first slog will run out of horizon before the hard semantics are correct.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between endpoints ad hoc with no ordering or done-conditions.
anchors.3: A flat endpoint checklist with no risk prioritization and no explicit 'done' criteria per item.
anchors.5: Clear milestones (boot+auth first, then resource groups, then the traps) with rough done-conditions, and recognizes the three traps as distinct workstreams.
anchors.8: Risk-aware sequencing: gets a bootable auth'd skeleton verifiable early, then deliberately front-loads or ring-fences the high-risk subsystems (idempotency serialization, webhook backoff/re-sign, PI state machine) as first-class milestones each with an explicit check, rather than burying them in CRUD.
anchors.10: Milestone structure that visibly de-risks the whole horizon: dependencies made explicit (e.g. PaymentIntent charges before refunds before subscription invoices), the trickiest semantics scheduled while budget remains, and the plan carries concrete acceptance conditions per milestone that later verification maps onto.

dimensions.name: SDK-driven, offline compatibility checks
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing how correctness is confirmed — exercising routes with the real `stripe` SDK / requests, and building targeted checks for idempotency, webhook retry, and state-machine edge cases — beyond 'it returns 200'.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Wire-level compatibility and the trap semantics fail silently; only active verification (ideally through the SDK the way the verifier will) distinguishes a plausible-looking response from a compliant one.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes endpoints work because the code was written.
anchors.3: Manual curl of a couple of happy paths; no SDK check, no coverage of error bodies or the trap behaviors.
anchors.5: Boots the service, smoke-tests health and several CRUD flows, and checks a few error/edge cases — but leaves the hardest semantics (concurrent idempotent retries, webhook backoff, illegal state transitions) largely unverified.
anchors.8: Verifies through the actual `stripe` SDK against `api_base`, and constructs specific checks for the traps: replaying an idempotency key (incl. a cached error body), same-key-different-body → 400, capturing a succeeded intent → 400, invalid PAN → decline, webhook 5xx retry/backoff.
anchors.10: A deliberate verification harness that covers happy paths, error envelopes, HTTP-code mappings, list pagination, restricted-key 403s, and the concurrency/temporal traps (serialized same-key retries never double-charge, re-signed late webhook deliveries), re-run after changes so regressions are caught rather than assumed away.

dimensions.name: Tracking coverage across a wide surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture over 12+ resource families and the trap subsystems, and detecting when effort is stuck or circling on one behavior.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With this much surface it is easy to lose the plot — over-polishing customers while subscriptions/invoices/webhooks remain unstarted, or re-debugging the same idempotency case repeatedly.

anchors.0: No sense of overall coverage; forgets whole resource families or repeats work.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; discovers late that major endpoints or the webhook worker were never implemented.
anchors.5: Keeps a running checklist of endpoints/subsystems and their status, and generally knows what remains.
anchors.8: Actively maintains coverage against the full route table, notices when stuck on one behavior and time-boxes it, and reallocates attention so no major area is silently dropped.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the whole horizon: distinguishes implemented-and-verified from implemented-only from missing, catches thrashing/circular debugging early and names it, and adjusts pace to land the full surface plus the traps within budget.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on compatibility failures
dimensions.description: Revising design/approach when SDK round-trips, error shapes, or trap semantics diverge from expectations — rather than pressing on with a falsified assumption.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reconstructing an external contract guarantees wrong initial assumptions (field names, signature scheme, state rules); the agent must let contradicting evidence rewrite the design, sometimes structurally (e.g. how idempotency serialization or the billing worker is built).

anchors.0: Ignores failing SDK calls or wrong outputs; keeps building on the broken assumption.
anchors.3: Patches surface symptoms (tweaks a field) without revisiting the underlying wrong model, so the same class of mismatch recurs.
anchors.5: When a check fails, diagnoses and fixes the root cause for that case and moves on.
anchors.8: Treats divergences as signals about the contract: on discovering e.g. a wrong signature format or state-transition rule, updates the mental model and propagates the fix across related endpoints, not just the one that failed.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven correction across the horizon, including structural pivots when needed (rethinking idempotency locking, webhook re-signing, or state-machine modeling once reality contradicts the plan), while preserving already-verified work — never barrels ahead on a falsified assumption.
